Symptoms: Sudden, uncontrollable episodes of laughing or crying, which may not match the individual's emotional state.

Symptoms: Headaches, visual disturbances, ringing in the ears (tinnitus), nausea, vomiting, and papilledema (swelling of the optic nerve).
Prevalence: Approximately 35 per 100,000 individuals in Italy; higher in females and obesity is a significant risk factor.
Annual_Therapy_Costs: Approximately 1,500 to 3,000 depending on treatment regimen and additional supportive care needed.
Quality_of_Life: Significantly affected due to chronic headaches and potential for vision impairment; many patients report difficulties in daily activities.

Safety: Generally welltolerated; longterm safety data remains limited.

Symptoms: Joint pain, stiffness, swelling, fatigue, plantar fasciitis, reduced range of motion, skin lesions, nail changes
Prevalence: Approximately 0.1% to 0.3% of the population in the USA is affected; about 50% of people with psoriasis may develop psoriatic arthritis.
Annual_Therapy_Costs: Estimated annual cost for TALTZ is approximately $70,000 to $80,000, depending on insurance coverage and patient copays.
Quality_of_Life: Psoriatic arthritis significantly impacts quality of life due to chronic pain, functional impairment, and psychological burden; many patients report a reduced quality of life compared to healthy individuals.
Efficacy: Clinical studies show that TALTZ can reduce signs and symptoms in 70% of patients, demonstrating strong efficacy in managing psoriatic arthritis.
Safety: Generally welltolerated; monitors for infections are recommended due to immunosuppressive effects but overall seen as safe for the majority of patients.
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events include injection site reactions, upper respiratory infections, nausea, and potential risk of serious infections (approximately 12%).
Age_Group: Approved for adults aged 18 years and older.
Gender: Affects both genders, but there is a slight male predominance in psoriatic arthritis prevalence.

Symptoms: Fatigue, jaundice, anemia, pale skin, shortness of breath, rapid heart rate, dark urine, enlarged spleen

Efficacy: Clinical trials demonstrate a significant increase in hemoglobin levels and a reduction in transfusion requirements for patients with pyruvate kinase deficiency
Safety: Generally welltolerated; longterm safety data is still being compiled as it is a newer therapy

Gender: Affects both males and females equally

Safety: Generally safe when used appropriately; however, allergic reactions can occur.

Symptoms: Abdominal pain, diarrhea, bloody stool, liver damage, and urinary problems. Chronic schistosomiasis can lead to serious complications such as liver fibrosis and bladder cancer.
Prevalence: Approximately 1.5 million cases diagnosed in the USA annually, primarily among travelers and immigrants from endemic countries.
Annual_Therapy_Costs: Approximately $10$20 for a single treatment course (may vary based on state and pharmacy pricing).
Quality_of_Life: Quality of life can be significantly affected due to chronic symptoms and complications if left untreated; patients may experience pain and limitations in daily activities.
Efficacy: Approximately 8590% effective in treating schistosomiasis when administered as a single dose.
Safety: Generally considered safe; however, caution is advised in those with severe liver impairment.
Adverse_Events: Common adverse events include dizziness, headache, fever, gastrointestinal discomfort, rash, and fatigue. Serious adverse events are rare.
Age_Group: All age groups; however, most prevalent in children and young adults due to risk factors associated with exposure.
Gender: Both genders are affected equally; however, risk factors may vary based on occupation or lifestyle.

Symptoms: Fatigue, swollen and bleeding gums, joint pain, anemia, skin issues (including rash and bruising), and poor wound healing.
Prevalence: Approximately 0.1% of the U.S. population is estimated to be affected by scurvy, with higher prevalence in certain groups, such as those with limited access to fresh fruits and vegetables.
Annual_Therapy_Costs: Estimated at $30 to $150, depending on the form and supplier of the supplement.
Quality_of_Life: Significantly decreased quality of life when symptomatic, but resolves rapidly with proper treatment.
Efficacy: High efficacy in alleviating symptoms of scurvy, with improvement typically seen within days of administration.
Safety: Generally safe with low risk of toxicity; excess in very high doses may cause gastrointestinal disturbances.
Adverse_Events: Rare; potential for diarrhea, nausea, and abdominal cramps in sensitive individuals.
Age_Group: All age groups, but especially observed in adults and the elderly who may not have adequate diets.
Gender: Both genders are equally affected by vitamin C deficiency.

Efficacy: GIAPREZA has been shown to improve blood pressure in patients with septic or neurogenic shock, with certain studies indicating a significant increase in mean arterial pressure
Safety: Generally considered safe; however, blood pressure should be closely monitored during administration
Adverse_Events: Hypotension, elevated blood pressure, tachycardia, and arrhythmias are noted adverse events
Age_Group: Primarily adults, but can be used in pediatric populations with careful monitoring

Symptoms: Fever, chills, loss of appetite, muscle pain, headaches, nausea, and abdominal pain; severe cases can lead to liver damage, bleeding, and organ failure.
Prevalence: Approximately 200,000 cases of yellow fever occur worldwide annually, with the majority in Africa and South America; in the USA, vaccination is recommended for travelers to endemic areas, but native cases are extremely rare.
Annual_Therapy_Costs: Approximately $150$300 for the vaccination, depending on provider and location, but variable since it may not be needed annually if vaccinated before traveling to endemic areas.
Quality_of_Life: Can be significantly affected in those who contract the disease, particularly during severe infection; survivors may experience longterm health issues.
Efficacy: Highly effective; one dose provides immunity in 95% of vaccinated individuals.
Safety: Generally safe; mild side effects are typical and include soreness at the injection site, fever, and headache. Serious side effects are rare.
Adverse_Events: Serious adverse events include allergic reactions and neurological disorders, but occur at a very low rate (approximately 1 in 100,000 to 1 in 1 million doses).
Age_Group: Recommended for individuals aged 9 months and older.
Gender: Both males and females are equally prone to vaccination and disease.
